# Five energy-draining contact branches

`draining.tsv` records actual ORANGE, FIRE, RED, PINK, and MAROON branches of the original private `touchEffects1` method.
Source twice and the bundled JAR produced identical bytes.
All four compiled helper classes also match across backends.
The fixture contains 449 cases, 901 snapshots, 2,703 actor views, and 452 actual calls.
Each actor view includes the complete 154-field organism observation schema.

## Comparison contract

The fixed ledger and typed input inventory precede Rust replay.
Compare nongeometric state, velocities, effects, gas, statistics, endpoints, bounds, ARGB, reactions, reference identity, ordering, and RNG exactly.
Only `_m`, `_m1`, `_m2`, `_mass`, and `_I` retain the existing organism geometry allowance.
For finite geometry, use `1e-10 * max(1, abs(expected))`.
Check geometric NaN classification and signed infinity explicitly.
Energy, byproducts, and other scalar results receive no additional tolerance.

Only `_world` and `_visibleWorld` are named organism collaborator exclusions.
Setup selection remains separate source callback-routing metadata.
Every other recorded observation remains a comparison obligation.
Full G/N blocks preserve every genome and gene value.
Whole-genome identity connects actor, infection, saved, and statistics references.
The separate genetics oracle covers per-Gene mutable-object alias topology.

## Actual execution and input authority

Compile `tools/reference/DrainOracle.java` against each pinned backend.
Run `biogenesis.DrainOracle NEW_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY` with the isolated arguments recorded in provenance.
The helper validates four explicit profile roots through `toRealPath` before accessing simulation state.
It rejects existing output directories and writes its new file with `CREATE_NEW`.
Six negative invocations cover each omitted root, an escaped profile symlink, and existing output preservation.
Positive processes have a 120-second bound; negative processes have a 30-second bound.
The existing runner cleans each owned process group.

Each case resets actual source defaults and records all 147 mutable primitive settings.
Initial organism attempts are zero; initial oxygen is `1000`.
Mutation bounds are `0..10000`; meta mutation is zero.
GREEN selection weight is seven; other selectable weights are zero.
The setup seed is `827364`.
No genesis or world frame executes.

Distinct supplied costs make the five weapon costs and three defensive costs distinguishable.

| Setting | Ordinary supplied value |
| --- | ---: |
| ORANGE energy consumption | 0.125 |
| FIRE energy consumption | 0.25 |
| RED energy consumption | 0.5 |
| PINK energy consumption | 1 |
| MAROON energy consumption | 2 |
| BLUE energy consumption | 0.375 |
| DODGE energy consumption | 0.625 |
| SKY energy consumption | 0.75 |

The source organic yield and ordinary byproduct proportion retain their defaults, `2` and `0.1`.
Labelled cases explicitly change costs, yield, byproduct proportion, or atmospheric oxygen.
All supplied settings appear in `U` before construction.

The helper creates real `VisibleWorld(null)` and World instances.
It invokes actual gas-add, organism construction, paste, and World.addOrganism methods.
Peer, victim, and killer are added in that order, at `(1000,1000)`, `(3500,3500)`, and `(2000,2000)`.
Their initial IDs are `0`, `1`, and `2`.
Peer is selected before the first add, avoiding MainWindow callback branches without mocks.
Actual contacts always use the distinct victim and killer objects.

Five original genotype identities are supplied before actor construction.
Ordinary `g0` contains two genes with the selected weapon color.
`g1` and `g2` ordinarily contain one GREEN gene.
Lengths are `12`; theta is `index * 0.25`.
The first branch is zero; subsequent branches are `-1`.
Symmetry is one, mirror is zero, and constructor booleans are false.
Generation is `41`; clade is `root`; all four modifiers initially equal one.
`g3` and `g4` ordinarily use actual GeneticCode.clone on `g0`.
The value-equal infection case instead clones `g1` into `g3`.
The shared-primary case pastes killer with the original `g0` reference.
Those recipe and actor-reference choices remain explicit `I/A` inputs.
No observed genotype or organism snapshot becomes a constructor input.

Setup controls supply victim and killer energy `1000`, active/alive flags, and cleared classification/dodge flags.
They clear the relevant version counters, kill/infection counters, and indigo values.
Both temporary colors begin MAGENTA with zero frames.
Photosynthesis begins at `10`; supplied photo coefficients are `index + 0.25`.
Victim initially holds `g3` as infection and `g4` as saved code.
Labelled cases supply each subsequent difference before its actual call.

The killer phenotype uses the selected current color while retaining its genuinely constructed body.
All explicit array controls must match the actual segment count.
Modified pink and cream controls mutate original GeneticCode fields.
Raw `_m` controls target the original per-segment length array.
These controlled states test methods; they do not assert natural contact eligibility or player UI acceptance.

## Source dispatch and coverage

Each `K` labels one of five operations: `touchEffects1.ORANGE`, `.FIRE`, `.RED`, `.PINK`, or `.MAROON`.
Before invocation, the helper verifies the selected actor segment has the exact labelled ARGB.
Reflection then invokes the original `touchEffects1(Organism,int,int)` method.
An unexpected actor color fails before the call.

The ordinary ORANGE sweep covers all 46 base colors, 18 internal colors, unknown ARGB, and translucent MAGENTA.
Other weapons use one representative per distinct source peer-case group.
The source inventory uses Java tokens and switch brace depth, independent of indentation.
Additional cases target nested decisions instead of multiplying every color by every flag combination.

| Baseline family | Cases | Source peer-case groups |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| ORANGE palette | 66 | 22 |
| FIRE representatives | 28 | 28 |
| RED representatives | 11 | 11 |
| PINK representatives | 13 | 13 |
| MAROON representatives | 16 | 16 |

The remaining 315 cases target classification, modifiers, payments, identities, death ordering, and numeric boundaries.
They include 120 bounded arithmetic/payment cases across the five distinct weapon costs and byproduct processes.

| Obligation | Actual observations |
| --- | --- |
| Classification | Plant, consumer, fungus, auburn, infectious, frozen, enhanced, transferred energy, and signed kill branches. |
| Modifiers | Both pink modifier pairs, cream modifier two, fallow versions, sky gates, and enhanced-peer exclusions. |
| Dodge | Full and partial defensive payments, already-marked peers, altruist exemptions, and RED's retained dodge state. |
| Shields | BLUE retaliation, failed BLUE/LIGHT_BLUE payments, SKY mutation, and enhanced FIRE/MAROON gates. |
| Infection | Shared references, value-equal distinct codes, shared primary codes, strong/weak fruit infection, and indigo guards. |
| Counters | Signed infection and kill wrapping, including both deaths from enhanced BLUE retaliation. |
| Byproducts | Ordinary respiration, PINK methane production, zero/full proportions, and incomplete later payments. |
| Bark | Active photosynthesis subtraction, inactive MAROON draining, enhanced bark exclusions, and selected segment one. |
| Old bark | First-contact tint priming, repeated draining, positive timers, active/inactive flags, and modifier-dependent coefficients. |
| Corpses | Live BROWN injury, enhanced exclusions, shifted age boundaries, wrapped maximum-age multiplication, and whole-energy draining. |
| Arithmetic | Negative, signed-zero, infinite, NaN, and genuinely constructed zero lengths; nonfinite energy and oxygen. |
| Death | Strict tolerance ties on ignored peer colors, counter/event ordering, and retained live statistics code aliases. |

The explicit source calls total 136 ORANGE, 108 FIRE, 50 RED, 81 PINK, and 77 MAROON invocations.
Three cases contain a second call: PINK priming, MAROON priming, and live statistics-code retention.
The last case changes the original dead peer's clade before another no-op contact.
Its statistics and full genotype observations retain the same actual code identity.

No new genotype or member appears.
The helper rejects unknown genotype references and unexpected member creation.
Every original gene value remains unchanged across snapshots.
Every case retains its original Random suffix through all actual calls.
`R` peeks through a serialized Random copy without consuming the live stream.

## Schema and row ledger

Rows retain the existing `C/U/I/A/P/K/O/H/W/S/T/G/N/R/E` schema.
Doubles use sixteen hexadecimal raw IEEE digits.
Arrays preserve comma-separated order; null references use `~`.
`K` contains stage, labelled operation, victim role, and `killer,segment,peer_segment`.
All actor views have 154 fields and three reference holders.
Every snapshot includes ten World values, 52 statistics fields, 49 getters, full G/N, and RNG suffix.

The provenance fixes every typed input target and each row count before Rust replay.
It records all three actual outputs, compiled classes, commands, exits, guards, and source hashes.
All 74 original hash/size/mode pins and 28 earlier TSVs remain unchanged.

The original Rust drain review and private tests cover hash `50d009b211fc081974040641921b570364bd5d6c2785aaedf03c7bc87640714a`.
Root later exposed only `age_bark` visibility for reuse.
Reversing that visibility marker reproduces the reviewed hash exactly.
The provenance attributes that separate change without transferring old private test claims to another hash.

This fixture does not execute contact detection, eligibility, complete frames, UI, networking, persistence migration, or distributable checks.
It does not demonstrate every combination of unrelated flags.
Java observation provenance does not claim Rust replay results.
